## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The stanzas of Thag 6.5 have extensive parallels across early Buddhist verse literature, particularly in collections treating craving (*taṇhā* / *tṛṣṇā*) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral identifies exact parallels in the Pali *Dhammapada* (Dhp 334–337), the *Patna Dharmapada* (*Tahnavagga*, vv. 137–156), the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (*Tṛṣṇavarga*, ch. 3) and its Tibetan counterpart, Chinese translations of the *Dharmapada* and *Udānavarga* (T 210.32, T 212.3, and T 213.3), and the *Uṭṭhāna Sutta* (Snp 2.10) [SuttaCentral]. Resembling verses also appear in the Gāndhārī Dharmapada (*Tasiṇavagga* and *Maguvagga*), the Sanskrit *Śarīrārthagāthā*, and the *Phandana-* and *Mahākapijātaka* (Ja 475, Ja 516) [SuttaCentral].
DharmaNexus detects substantial Pali-internal text reuse between Thag 6.5 (§0.4–4.6) and the *Dhammapada* (§334.0.4–337.6), as well as corresponding citations in the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* and *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records cross-language alignments with high plausibility scores to the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* and the *Patna Dharmapada*, confirming the canonical parallels recorded by SuttaCentral, alongside lower-scoring machine matches to the Tibetan *Susthitamatidevaputraparipṛcchāsūtra* (D0080) [DharmaNexus].
